constant-log-slope.problem: Given that $y=@@constant@@-@@a@@{log}_{@@base@@}x$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}@@base@@}.$
constant-log-slope.solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(@@constant@@-@@a@@{log}_{@@base@@}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(@@constant@@)-@@a@@\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{@@base@@}x) \\  & =0-@@a@@\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@} \\  & =-\frac{@@a@@}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1/\operatorname{ln}@@base@@$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1/\operatorname{ln}@@base@@} & ={(-\frac{@@a@@}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@})\,|}_{x=1/\operatorname{ln}@@base@@} \\  & =-\frac{@@a@@}{1} \\  & =-@@a@@.\end{aligned}
$$

scaled-log.solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{xln⁡a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(@@a@@{log}_{@@base@@}⁡x) \\  & =@@a@@\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{@@base@@}⁡x) \\  & =@@a@@\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡@@base@@} \\  & =\frac{@@a@@}{xln⁡@@base@@}.\end{aligned}
$$

quadratic-slope.solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(@@a@@{x}^{2}-@@b@@{log}_{@@base@@}x) \\  & =@@a@@\cdot 2x-@@b@@\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@} \\  & =@@two_a@@x-\frac{@@b@@}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(@@two_a@@x-\frac{@@b@@}{x\operatorname{ln}@@base@@})|}_{x=1} \\  & =@@two_a@@(1)-\frac{@@b@@}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}@@base@@} \\  & =@@two_a@@-\frac{@@b@@}{\operatorname{ln}@@base@@}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

log-minus-ln.solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{@@base@@}x-@@b@@\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{@@base@@}x)-@@b@@\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(@@base@@)}-@@b@@(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(@@base@@)}-\frac{@@b@@}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡a}.
